claims.text: Failure modes (gap found and fixed): a request carrying a body that the server never reads had its body parsed as a second request on the same keep-alive connection. Now any non-GET request, or one with Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding, closes its connection after one answer. Before the fix a probe got 2 responses for one POST; the new test asserts exactly 1.
claims.proof_output: pre-fix probe: '2 responses on smuggle'; post-fix: test_an_unread_body_is_never_parsed_as_a_second_request passed

claims.text: Failure modes (gap found and fixed): the handler had no socket timeout (probe printed 'handler timeout None'), so an idle or half-sent request held a thread forever. _Handler.timeout = 30; a test with the timeout lowered shows a half-sent request's connection closed.

Failure modes: port in use -> next free loopback port; none free in range -> NoFreePort, which `cma review` reports as a case-store refusal (exit 2); unknown case -> exit 2 'no case'; binding anything but 127.0.0.1 is refused.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest tests/test_review_server.py -q -k 'port or loopback or unknown_case'

claims.text: Idempotency / data: the server is read-only (GET only, 405 for every other method), writes nothing to the case folder, and adds no stored data, so there is no migration and nothing to reverse; a new token per launch (each start is independent).

Observability: `cma review` prints the URL with its token on start and 'Review workspace stopped.' on exit, proven end to end in a subprocess that reads the URL, gets 200 with the token and 403 without.
Regression: full suite, ruff and compileall pass with the hardening; contracts tier passes.
